answer: One concrete defense is to make each identity carry a costly, verifiable history: an agent must lock a small stake in a shared vault before it can trade, and that stake is slashed if peers detect duplicate behavior. Every action then leaves a public thread of attestations linking reputation to one identity, so a sybil swarm cannot fake trust cheaply. Like a tundra crossing, the path is slow and exposed, so creating many fake agents costs more than any single scam can return, making honest participation the rational choice.
